scenes.headline: How decision models found four new places to run
scenes.sub: An image API, six open sizes, a laptop and a local server.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tortellini! This week, decision models learned where to run: an image API, six open sizes, a laptop, and a local server.

scenes.text: A decision model scores every option you offer in one forward pass. This week the same request shape works everywhere it runs.
scenes.say: A decision model scores every option in one pass, writing no text. This week, one request shape works everywhere.

steps.say: In the local server, you send a state and typed questions to one endpoint, in Jev's own format.
Behind it sit six readouts, one per model family: letter logits, a pointer, or a joint head.
Each raw score is scaled by a stored temperature and softmaxed. One family reads each choice twice, in both orders.
The open family writes a question and its options into one prompt, and runs the backbone once.
It keeps the hidden state at the end of every option, and at the final token.
A small shared head scores each option against the question. No temperature is fitted afterwards.

scenes.title: Five questions, one call, on a laptop
scenes.say: The laptop port packs every question into one call.

items.say: The shared context is read once.
Each question attends to that prefix and itself, never to the others.
Five answers come back from one call, on the graphics chip.

scenes.text: Decision models now run almost anywhere. None of this week's releases tells you how often they are right.

scenes.say: To recap: one endpoint, one shared head, and accuracy left for you to measure.
